cases.name: List versions; version info
cases.notes: Lists and resolves real versions from the version manager, filtered by the access policy (private versions are visible to owner/admin only). A non-visible version returns 404 rather than 403, so existence is not leaked; an invalid GUID returns 400. Providers without versioning return an empty list rather than an error.

cases.name: Alter version; delete version
cases.notes: Alter updates name/access/description; delete removes the version and returns 409 rather than deleting mid-reconcile/post. Both are owner-or-admin gated. The returned moment is wall-clock time, not a branch generation.

cases.name: Reconcile; post; resolveConflicts; inspectConflicts
cases.notes: Real reconcile/post over the Postgres version manager: conflictResolution/resolutionPolicy/abortIfConflicts and conflictDetection (including the Esri tokens) are honoured, withPost=true posts inline, and async=true returns 202 with a pollable job; lock contention returns 409 and an unsupported policy 400. inspectConflicts returns the pending conflict set with three-way base/DEFAULT/version images and per-field diffs; resolveConflicts applies per-feature {layerId, objectId, choice} resolutions. Providers without versioning return 501 rather than fabricating success.

cases.name: Version job status
cases.notes: Polls the durable job runner for an async reconcile/post; a job GUID belonging to another service or version returns 404.

cases.name: Service metadata
cases.notes: Returns a hardcoded descriptor (defaultVersionName "sde.DEFAULT", capabilities "Create,Delete,Alter,Reconcile,Post") after a service-read check only. It does not consult the provider's versioning support, so a non-Postgres store advertises five capabilities whose mutations then return 501.

cases.name: Create version
cases.notes: Creates a real version and maps a duplicate name to 409, but parentVersion is accepted and ignored (always null), so a version can only be branched from DEFAULT.

cases.name: startReading; stopReading; startEditing; stopEditing
cases.notes: Stateless acknowledgements: Honua holds no Esri edit/read session and issues no session token, because edits land per-request via gdbVersion rather than inside a server-held session. startEditing does resolve the version, return its durable branch generation as moment, and return 409 mid-reconcile/post; stopEditing has no saveEdits semantics (there is nothing to commit or discard). A client that depends on session tokens will not get Esri's behaviour.

cases.name: no Esri edit/read session model: start/stop Reading/Editing are stateless acknowledgements with no session token
create ignores parentVersion, so versions branch only from DEFAULT
service metadata hardcodes its capabilities and does not reflect provider versioning support
branch versioning is backed by Postgres only; other providers return 501 on mutations
